findings.title: Unsubscribe 500s when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id, topic_id) and immediately reads tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when that logged-in user has no topic_users row for the topic (never opened it, a different account than the email recipient, or the row was removed). Calling notification_level on nil raises NoMethodError, so the new email link returns 500 instead of unsubscribing or rendering the page. Email delivery usually inserts a row via TopicUser.change, but this public route does not, and nothing here creates one. Use TopicUser.change (it inserts when missing) or handle a missing record, and still persist an explicit muted level.

findings.title: Unsubscribe does not stop notifications for watching or tracking
findings.body: The email string says the link will "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic", and the page string says "You will stop receiving notifications". The action does not do that. Levels are muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3. If the level is above regular it is set to regular; only regular or muted is set to muted. Tracking and regular send the same reply, mention, and quote emails, so a tracking user who clicks the link is unchanged and keeps those emails. A watching user is only dropped to regular and still gets reply, mention, and quote mail for the topic. The GET is also not idempotent: a refresh or second fetch sees regular and then mutes, so the result depends on how many times the URL is hit, and neither the email nor the page describes a two-step downgrade. The client route never changes the level itself, so an in-app transition to /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe only shows that future-tense copy. To match the copy, one request should set the topic to muted.

findings.title: Direct save lets auto-track undo the unsubscribe
findings.body: The action assigns notification_level and calls save!. TopicUser.change is what records a user-chosen level: it sets notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed when it is still nil, and publishes on MessageBus. save! does none of that. update_last_read's SQL and TopicUser.auto_track only auto-upgrade a topic to tracking when notifications_reason_id is null. A row created just to store last_emailed_post_number still has a null reason. After this sets muted or regular, the next read that crosses an enabled auto-track threshold (user auto_track_topics_after_msecs or the site setting >= 0) writes tracking back, so the unsubscribe does not stick and notifications resume. Other open tabs also keep the old level because MessageBus is not notified. Persist the change through TopicUser.change so it is stored as an explicit user choice.

findings.title: Topic unsubscribe mutates notification level on GET
findings.body: config/routes.rb exposes GET /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe and GET /t/:topic_id/unsubscribe, and the action writes notification_level before rendering. There is no per-user token and no CSRF token. The URL is predictable from the topic slug and id, and protect_from_forgery does not apply to GET. In this app's era, browsers send session cookies on cross-site GETs, so another site can change a logged-in user's topic level with an img, redirect, or top-level link. A prefetch that includes the session does the same without a click. Because the downgrade is not idempotent, two fetches can go from watching to regular and then to muted. Do not change state on GET; show a confirmation and mutate on POST, or require an unguessable one-time key plus an explicit confirm.

findings.title: Shared render drops canonical URL on every topic page
findings.body: show calls perform_show_response and only then calls canonical_url(...) with the topic canonical path, discarding the return value. That call exists to store the URL the layout emits (Discourse assigns @canonical_url for rel=canonical / og:url) before render. Rendering used to be implicit at the end of the action, after that call. This change adds render :show inside perform_show_response's HTML branch, which show and unsubscribe both use, so the topic template and layout run before canonical_url. Every normal topic HTML response is sent without its canonical link. That is an SEO regression for all topic pages, not just unsubscribe. Set the canonical URL before rendering, or render only from unsubscribe after show's post-setup has run.

findings.title: Unsubscribe template path does not match the Ember route
findings.body: app-route-map.js.es6 registers a top-level route named topicUnsubscribe at /t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe. Ember resolves that route's template from the dasherized name topic-unsubscribe (underscore/dasherize of topicUnsubscribe, not a slash path). The new route, controller, and view files use that name (topic-unsubscribe.js.es6), but the template is templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs, which is registered as topic/unsubscribe — the name for a nested topic.unsubscribe route that was never defined. After the server handles the email link, the Ember app will not find a template and will error instead of showing the confirmation text and the topic-notifications-button. Put the template at templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs, or nest the route as topic.unsubscribe and move the controller and view to match.

findings.title: No spec checks unsubscribe behavior or the new email link
findings.body: The only spec change passes unsubscribe_url into MessageBuilder so the updated unsubscribe_link translation does not raise MissingInterpolationArgument, then still only asserts that the user-preferences URL is in the body. It never checks that the topic unsubscribe URL or the new "stop receiving notifications about this particular topic" sentence is present. There is no controller or request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe: missing TopicUser, watching versus tracking versus regular, a second request stepping down again, the slug redirect, or notifications_reason_id being set. Those paths are currently untested and are where this feature fails.
